papers.title: 2.3-kV Vertical GaN Trench MOSFET With Variable Lateral Ion-Implanted Guard Rings
papers.summary: This letter presents a vertical GaN trench MOSFET featuring Variable Lateral Ion-implanted Guard Rings (VLGR) formed in a partially thinned p-GaN region to engineer the edge electric field distribution. The proposed graded termination effectively mitigates electric field crowding, enabling a breakdown voltage ( BV ) of 2305 V—an approximately 2.7-fold improvement over the Ref-MOSFET (850 V). The fabricated device exhibits a threshold voltage ( ${V}_{\text {TH}}\text {)}$ of 4.9 V, a specific on-resistance ( ${R}_{\text {on, sp}}\text {)}$ of 7.2 m $\Omega \cdot $ cm 2 , and an on/off current ratio of $10^{{7}}$ , yielding a Baliga’s figure of merit ( BFOM ) of 738 MW/cm 2 . These results demonstrate an effective edge-termination strategy for extending the blocking capability of fully vertical GaN trench MOSFETs and suggest the potential of this structure for high-voltage power electronics applications.

papers.title: Novel Unipolar Stacked FET (USFET) Architecture Enabled by Tri-Layer Dummy Gate, Quasi-GAA SD Process, and Interconnect Innovations
papers.summary: In this work, a novel unipolar stacked FET (USFET) is proposed, featuring nFET-on-nFET or pFET-on-pFET stacking with split gate (SG). From the perspective of process complexity, USFET shows a distinct advantage over complementary FET (CFET) by adopting a quasi-gate-all-around (GAA) source/drain (SD) process. Furthermore, a tri-layer dummy gate (TDG) process is proposed to simplify the SG process. This process can also be extended to CFET to facilitate the integration of heterogeneous channels and different gate stacks. From the perspective of interconnect design, a common-SD (CSD) structure can be incorporated in USFET, and its area efficiency and routing complexity can be optimized simultaneously. By integrating these innovations, USFET shows superior performance in both area scaling and electrical performance. Additionally, the USFET enables wider bit-line (BL)/BLB for further optimization. Compared to CFET, USFET static random access memory (SRAM) with wider BL/BLB (USFET WBL ) delivers a 23.1% area reduction, a $2.8\times $ higher write margin (WM), and decreases read and write delays by 19.1%/25.1% (frontside/backside) and 32.4%, respectively, proving its potential for advanced nodes.

papers.title: Monolithic Integration of Mg-Free Trench-Gate MOSFETs and μ LEDs
papers.summary: Driven by the rapid development of augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) displays, micro light-emitting diode ( $\mu $ LED) technology is evolving toward high brightness, high refresh rate, and high pixel density, which conventional driving and driving integration schemes can hardly meet. GaN-based monolithic drive-display integration is promising, yet existing schemes are limited by Mg doping-induced issues, poor process compatibility and high fabrication complexity. This work proposed and realized monolithically integrated Mg-free trench-gate metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) and $\mu $ LEDs, which deliver a specific on-resistance of ~15.4 m $\Omega \cdot $ cm 2 and an on/off current ratio of $\sim {5}\times {10} ^{{6}}$ , alongside turn-on/off delays of 300 ns/30 ns measured at 100 kHz. By replacing conventional Mg doping with polarization-induced doping, this approach offers high process compatibility and low fabrication complexity, paving a novel route for monolithic integration of GaN transistors and $\mu $ LEDs.

papers.title: 1700-V Enhancement-Mode MIS-HEMTs With Fully Recessed-Gate on 6-in GaN-on-Si Wafer
papers.summary: Enhancement-mode (E-mode) devices are preferred in power electronics for intrinsic fail-safe operation. Among mainstream approaches to fabricate E-mode GaN-based high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs), cascode structures are limited by Si-based devices, while p-GaN gate structures suffer from low gate breakdown voltage (BV) and constrained threshold voltage ( ${\mathrm{V}}_{\text {th}}\text {)}$ . To realize E-mode GaN-based HEMTs with high BV and robust reliability under high electric-field stress, we fabricated devices integrated with stepped fully recessed-gate structure and multilayer SiN dielectric on a 6-in GaN/Si wafer, which exhibited a high V th of 2.6 V and a large off -state BV of 1763 V. Meanwhile, a low gate interface trap density of $5.5\times 10^{{11}}$ ${\mathrm{cm}}^{-{2}}~\cdot $ ${\mathrm{eV}}^{-{1}}$ at ${\mathrm{E}}_{\text {C}} -$ ${\mathrm{E}}_{\text {T}}=0.455$ eV was obtained, yielding a significant improvement of the device reliability. A small V th shift of merely 0.2 V was achieved under 6-V positive gate bias stress for 3 h, and the dynamic on -resistance of the fabricated E-mode HEMTs is only 1.3 times larger than the static one even under an ultrahigh drain bias stress of 900 V. These results fully validate the attractive potential of the proposed scheme in developing high-voltage-rated GaN-based E-mode power devices toward various engineering applications.

papers.title: Area-Efficient and High-Performance 3T CFET Cells Enabled by an Embedded Interconnect Layer (EI-CFET) With Sequential Integration
papers.summary: Complementary FET (CFET) architectures are promising for logic scaling, especially when combined with backside power delivery networks (BSPDNs). In this work, we propose a CFET architecture featuring an embedded interconnect (EI) layer (EI-CFET), enabled by sequential process integration. By redistributing signal and power routing across the frontside (FS), EI layer, and backside (BS), the proposed architecture enables a 3T standard-cell height (CH) and reduces the cell area by approximately 25% and 20% relative to the 4T and 3.75T FS-/BS-routed reference CFET cells, respectively. The EI layer alleviates routing-induced parasitic penalties by shortening critical connections and improving routing flexibility, leading to more pronounced performance benefits in cells with denser internal routing. Meanwhile, connection failures induced by top-to-bottom misalignment can be effectively mitigated by an optimized EI handoff structure, and the performance variation is suppressed to below 0.5%. In addition, independent crystallographic optimization of stacked devices provides additional performance gains exceeding 6% over the reference design. These results demonstrate that the EI-CFET is a promising candidate for high-density and high-performance 3-D CMOS technologies.

papers.title: Avalanche Failure Mechanism of SiC MOSFETs After Total Ionizing Dose Irradiation
papers.summary: This brief reports the impact of total ionizing dose (TID) irradiation on the avalanche behavior of SiC MOSFETs. Experimental results show that the avalanche energy ( ${E}_{\textit {av}}\text {)}$ decreases by 5.99% and 13.83%, while the threshold voltage ( ${V}_{\textit {TH}}\text {)}$ shifts negatively by 34.14% and 76.34% after 50 krad and 100 krad TID irradiation, respectively. Both microscopic analysis and TCAD simulation results indicate that the diversion of avalanche current from the body diode to the MOS channel underlies this degradation. Due to the irradiation-induced accumulation of positive charges in the gate oxide, ${V}_{\textit {TH}}$ exhibits a negative shift with increasing irradiation dose. As a result, the margin for fully turning off the MOS channel under a fixed gate-off voltage ( ${V}_{\textit {GS}\_{\textit {off}}}\text {)}$ during avalanche is reduced, and a portion of the avalanche current is redirected from the body diode to the adjacent MOS channel. As channel mobility is low in SiC MOSFETs, this current diversion generates substantial Joule heating and triggers a rapid temperature rise along the channel path. Ultimately, premature burnout occurs in SiC MOSFETs after TID irradiation during avalanche. This finding provides insights into reliability assessment and radiation hardening of SiC MOSFETs for space applications.

papers.title: Achieving 0.82-dB NF min in High-Drain-Bias GaN HEMTs via Buffer and Field-Plate Engineering for High-Linearity LNA Applications
papers.summary: In this letter, minimum noise figure ( NF ${}_{\text{min} }$ ) of GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) under high-drain bias ( $\textit{V}_{\text {DS}} \gt \text{20}$ V) is investigated and optimized for high-linearity low noise amplifier (LNA) applications. By employing a $\text{1}~\mu $ m Fe-doped GaN buffer and a non-overlapping source field plate (SFP), the device achieves a NF min of 0.82 dB at 3 GHz and a $\textit{V}_{\text {DS}}$ of 24 V, while delivering an associated gain ( $\textit{G}_{\text {a}}$ ) of 16.61 dB and an output third-order intercept point (OIP3) of 31.8 dBm. Experimental comparison and a physics-based noise model identify the sharp increase in gate leakage current ( $\textit{I}_{\text {G}}$ ) as the dominant cause of NF min degradation under high $\textit{V}_{\text {DS}}$ , and confirm its suppression using $\text{1}~\mu $ m Fe-doped buffer scheme. Moreover, a non-overlapping SFP suppresses the device’s thermal noise by lowering the intrinsic resistances ( $\textit{R}_{\text {i}}$ , $\textit{R}_{\text {gd}}$ ). This work provides a novel design optimization strategy for high-bias, low-noise GaN HEMTs tailored for high-linearity LNA applications.

papers.title: All-GaN Monolithic 2T1C- μ LED Pixel With MHz Optical Modulation for High-Refresh-Rate Microdisplays
papers.summary: High-refresh-rate active-matrix microdisplays are essential components for many high-end applications, such as augmented reality (AR) displays. In this work, an all-GaN monolithic active micro-light-emitting diode ( $\mu $ LED) pixel with optical modulation up to 2 MHz is demonstrated. The pixel consists of one $20~\mu $ m-diameter $\mu $ LED, two depletion-mode GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs), and one metal-insulator-metal (MIM) storage capacitor (2T1C), with a total footprint of $60~\mu $ m $\times 60~\mu $ m. The GaN-based 2T1C-driven circuit is integrated monolithically with $\mu $ LEDs formed via selective-area growth (SAG) without sidewall etching. Static performance of the 2T1C- $\mu $ LED circuit has been tested under different ${V}_{\text {Data}}$ conditions. Transient measurements show its capability for “write-on, hold-on, write-off, and hold-off” operation, with both electrical and optical modulation up to 2 MHz, indicating great potential for high-end AR microdisplays.
